item: the narrowed engine identity falls back to the whole store.py on module-data mutation setattr and local-def decorators
summary: Follow-on to the narrowed engine identity: the digest now returns None (hash the whole file) when any def calls a mutating method (append/update/add/pop/clear ...) on module-level data, calls setattr/delattr, or is decorated by one of the module's own defs (a decorator registry), because such a def can change what index_article reads without being reachable by name. Replay over the last 24 store.py commits unchanged (7 keep the id, 17 move it, 0 fallbacks) and the real file still narrows. Also covers names bound by a top-level import (os.environ.update), mutating methods on class attributes and decorators rooted at module-level objects. Stated limits: a store through a local alias, a returned nonlocal closure and a non-listed method on a module-level instance (_S.set_mode) are not caught; none exists in store.py. Tests: 12 new parametrized fallbacks.
